origin: docs/CWE-502/python Common Pitfalls: Replacing pickle in HTTP handlers but leaving shelve, pandas pickle files, task queues, or cache loaders unchanged

finding.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
finding.summary: a cache entry selected by a request-supplied model name is deserialized with pickle

trap: Replacing pickle.loads() with json.loads(), which the entry's Remediation Steps lead with. The nightly batch job that populates this cache still pickles a full model object exposing .predict(); JSON has no representation for it, so switching only the reader leaves every legitimately cached entry unreadable without addressing which entries an attacker can reach or substitute.
must_preserve: get_prediction still returns a JSON body with a prediction key computed by calling .predict() on the cached model object for an existing model name, and still responds 404 when the cache entry is absent.
